races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Furturra
runners_data.comment: Dominant at Redcar last time, drawing clear of a novice field by five lengths to take his second win in recent starts; he concedes weight to every rival today which is the one check on his prospects, but he has clearly found his feet over 5-6f on good ground and the form reads well.

runners_data.name: Aodhan
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on his only start at Redcar last week, he appeared to need the run and should come on considerably for it; rated lowest of the field here, he needs a substantial step forward to make any impression.

runners_data.name: Bigalo
runners_data.comment: Short of his debut level when beaten ten lengths in a novice at Ripon last time, this is his second consecutive modest effort; a major turnaround in form would be required to play a part here.

runners_data.name: Cagney
runners_data.comment: An Earthlight colt purchased for £65,000, he is a half-brother to a useful 6f performer and his dam showed smart form over the same trip as a juvenile; the yard has a good record with first-time runners at this course, and he is well regarded for this debut despite a quiet recent spell for the trainer.

runners_data.name: Casino Star
runners_data.comment: Runner-up on debut, finishing with running to spare and looking like a colt who will improve for the experience; effective at 6f on good to soft and given a solid chance here with normal progression, he shapes as a genuine danger from stall 1.

runners_data.name: Mezzo Forte
runners_data.comment: A Wootton Bassett colt out of a dam who showed high-class form at 6-7f as a juvenile — including at Group 3 level — he arrives with a top jockey/trainer partnership operating in fine form and is taken seriously for this debut; breeding and market support will both be worth watching.

runners_data.name: Rbflying
runners_data.comment: Beaten eight and a half lengths in a maiden at Hamilton last time, running to a similar level as on debut; stepping up to 6f could help, but a significant improvement is needed to make an impression here.

runners_data.name: Sirocco Sands
runners_data.comment: Fourth in a maiden at the Curragh last time, beaten just over two lengths in useful form; suits 5-6f on soft or good to yielding ground and there could be more to come, making him one to respect for a lightly raced colt who has shown ability across both starts.

runners_data.name: Sue's Last Chance
runners_data.comment: Beaten three lengths in a maiden at York last time in a run that suggested he shaped with more promise than his position implies; acts on good ground and 7f may suit even better, and he could still go well here, though he remains yet to score and needs another forward step to threaten.

runners_data.name: Washington Royale
runners_data.comment: A Washington DC colt and half-brother to a very useful 7f performer, his opening price is worth monitoring on debut; no racecourse experience to go on, but the breeding suggests he could surprise.

runners_data.name: Yorkshire Dream
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a novice at Carlisle last time in a run that fell short of his debut level; his best form has come at 5f on good to firm ground, which raises a small question about today's trip, and a clear improvement is required to be competitive here.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Mary
runners_data.comment: Fourth in a claimer at Beverley last time when outpaced over too short a trip, the step back up in distance is in her favour; she acts at 5f on good to firm and there is plenty to find on our figures, with the jump in class also significant.

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Mile Handicap

runners_data.name: Wahdan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Tim Easterby whose best recent form on Good ground came at 9f-10f — dropping to a flat mile here is a concern, and while the trainer has a strong 8/90 strike-rate over 14 days, the form string of 8530-8 is uninspiring; needs a strong pace to deliver late.
runners_data.comment: Keen in defeat when beaten six lengths at the course 15 days ago, he was never able to land a blow from off the pace in that handicap; a return to the bare mile may suit, though he remains without a win in recent starts and the mid-field ranking reflects a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Darkness
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up specialist for David O'Meara wearing a visor, with solid course form but predominantly a 7f horse on Good — stepping up to a mile is a notable query, and 10 of 15 similar-going runs have resulted in double-figure finishes; needs things to fall perfectly.
runners_data.comment: First-time visor applied for a gelding who has failed to get into races from off the pace in recent outings, including when beaten six lengths here last time; his speed figures are solid and he suits 7f on any going, but he needs to show a good deal more to justify faith.

runners_data.name: Wild Nature
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner for Edward Bethell, and Oisin Murphy will look to exploit that role from stall draw; the STYLE_FIT tag at 0.93 suggests this trip and role is slightly outside its comfort zone as a 7f performer, and six of 11 similar-going runs have been mid-field finishes; key to the whole race shape.
runners_data.comment: Third at Musselburgh most recently, though that run was well off his best after a return from a break; suits 7-8f on a sound surface and he could do considerably better than that, with the jockey booking an additional reason for interest following a break of over five weeks.

runners_data.name: Sujet
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll's four-year-old has placed from prominent positions at 7f on Good ground twice in last five, and Zak Wheatley takes over; the form shows a troubled run on debut at this trip but two placed efforts at the track on Good are encouraging and this type of race suits.
runners_data.comment: Returning to a mile could be the key for a gelding who shaped poorly when beaten nine lengths in a handicap here last time; effective at 7-9f on soft and good ground and yet to score in recent starts, though the trip switch gives him a chance to improve on that.

runners_data.name: Jimmy Speaking
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes over for Chris Dwyer on a horse that has won at 7f on Standard and placed at 8f on Good — the two recent wins give confidence; a prominent runner who has the tactical speed to sit just behind Wild Nature and kick off a sustainable gallop.
runners_data.comment: With two wins in recent starts to his name and facing an identical official mark here, the drop to the bare mile should suit a gelding effective at 7-8f on any going; from stall 13 but consistent on a variety of surfaces, he is not without prospects at this level.

runners_data.name: Frankies Dream
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee partners this Jennie Candlish four-year-old who wears headgear (hood) and has placed in three of last four — all on Good ground at 8f-9f — confirming the surface and trip suit; a genuine prominent type with a consistent placed record.
runners_data.comment: Wearing a hood for the first time, he finished with purpose when narrowly beaten here last time off a mark 2lb lower than today's — strong form from a gelding who has been knocking at the door; the drop to a bare mile is a mild concern for one best at 7-9f, but he is clearly in good heart.

runners_data.name: Andesite
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's four-year-old wears a tongue-tie and has placed twice in Good-ground runs at 7f-8f; Kevin Stott is an established booking and the horse has hold-up tendencies that could suit a well-run race — the step up from 7f to a flat mile looks workable based on the 8f placed run.
runners_data.comment: Rated top of the field and in consistent form, he ran with credit at this course last time when beaten just two lengths off a mark 1lb below today's, typically held up for a late run; a tongue-tie applied for the first time and he steps from stall 15.

runners_data.name: Cadarn
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's five-year-old is a natural prominent racer but the field congestion means Shane Gray will likely be unable to get that forward position — 14 of last five starts contain double-digit finishes in similar going, and the tongue-tie is retained; discount its chance sharply given the STYLE_FIT and redistribution flags.
runners_data.comment: Outpaced over ten furlongs at this track most recently, the drop back to 7-8f is a clear positive; absent 43 days and wearing a tongue-tie for the first time, he has shown his best form on faster ground and the all-weather, so there is a question whether today's going fully plays to his strengths.

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ryley
runners_data.note: Alan Brown's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear — David Nolan rides a horse whose last five runs are all at 6f, making this step up to a flat mile a significant trip query on top of the style compromise.
runners_data.comment: Beaten thirteen lengths at the course last time when stepped up in trip and contributing little, he remains 6lb above his last winning mark even with this 1lb drop; his best form has come at 6-7f on any going and a substantial upturn is needed.

runners_data.name: Eligible
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's ten-year-old is a front-runner by nature but there is simply no room at the head of this field for another prominent type; Lewis Chalkley (7lb claim) rides, but age, the crowded pace scenario, and six blank similar-going runs make this a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: Never landing a blow from off the pace when beaten five lengths here last time, stepping back up in trip should suit a gelding effective at 7-8f; on a mark that looks workable and acts on any going, so there is a reasonable case, though our figures have him ranked towards the lower end of this field.

runners_data.name: Zennor Storm
runners_data.note: William Haggas three-year-old with just four runs, two of which were wins on Standard ground — form on Good proper is limited to two unplaced runs; Tom Marquand takes over and the OR=87 rating makes this one to respect on potential, though the prominent draw in a congested field complicates things.
runners_data.comment: A colt who won both his early starts on the all-weather convincingly but has struggled to produce that level in two subsequent outings on turf, most recently beaten six lengths in a handicap; now gelded, and with a respected jockey/trainer combination for this course aboard, there are grounds to think he can rediscover his earlier ability.

runners_data.name: Golden Strike
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's five-year-old is a serial front-runner wearing blinkers who has won three of last five, all at 7f on Good or Standard — Oisin Orr rides, but this horse cannot get its natural position and being pushed back into midfield cuts right across its game plan; form when unable to lead is poor.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap here last time, getting the better of a tight finish off a mark 3lb below today's and finishing with real purpose; now wearing a visor for the first time 35 days later, the rise in the weights is the obvious concern for a gelding most effective at 6-7f, but the course form is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Tailgunner Joe
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's three-year-old for Jonny Peate has a consistent hold-up profile — six recent runs include one win at 8f on Good, though the preponderance of mid-field and rear finishes on Good going (11 of 13 similar-going runs) suggests the horse struggles to quicken off a fair pace.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Epsom last time in a run that continues a disappointing recent sequence; remains capable at 7-9f on soft or fast ground and the mark is gradually easing, but he needs a significant change in fortunes to figure in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Blue To Blue
runners_data.note: Ruth Jefferson's three-year-old has won at 7f and placed at 8f on Good, which is an encouraging profile for this race — Billy Garritty rides and the horse is a genuine prominent type whose two placed runs at 8f on Good are directly relevant; a well-handicapped runner if it can travel into the race.
runners_data.comment: Below his recent best when beaten six lengths at Carlisle last time, a bounce back is needed to feature here; suits 7-8f on a sound surface and has shown he can compete at this level, but he needs to recapture his better form having gone off the boil most recently.

runners_data.name: Delinquent
runners_data.note: K R Burke's three-year-old has won twice at 8f, carries headgear (hood), and Cam Hardie knows the horse — but this is a natural prominent type that cannot get its position in this 16-runner field, and the STYLE_FIT of 0.90 is the lowest in the race; Burke's trainer yard is firing (13/46 over 14 days) but the positional handicap is real.
runners_data.comment: Second in our ratings and wearing first-time cheekpieces, he ran his race when fifth off the same mark last time, and a trainer working at 28% over the past fortnight is a noteworthy ally; effective at 7-8f on fast ground and shapes as a genuine contender.

runners_data.name: Nostrum
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — disregard for race analysis purposes.

races.paceDynamic: Wild Nature is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with Oisin Murphy aboard, will likely bowl along at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over this flat York mile — not a searching pace, but enough to keep the field honest. The field is loaded with prominent-types (Sujet, Jimmy Speaking, Frankies Dream, Zennor Storm, Blue To Blue) who will be fighting for positions just off the leader, while Cadarn, Eligible, Golden Strike and Delinquent are genuine front-runners who cannot all get there and will be shuffled back into mid-division against their natural instincts. With those displaced runners cluttering the middle of the field and hold-up horses like Wahdan, Darkness, Andesite and Tailgunner Joe needing clear runs, this shapes as a well-strung-out, processional race where the pace is genuine but not injurious. The tactical verdict is clear: horses that can travel prominently just off Wild Nature — getting a true but not brutal gallop to aim at — are best placed, particularly those with a proven turn of foot on Good ground at this sort of trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Nature sets a sustainable pace and the legitimate prominent horses track closely, producing a decisive front-end finish.
scenarios.body: If Wild Nature sets a sustainable pace and the legitimate prominent horses track closely, producing a decisive front-end finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Splits
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough to stretch the field and create a gap for a well-timed late run down the York straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just fast enough to stretch the field and create a gap for a well-timed late run down the York straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Nature fails to sustain the gallop and the prominent scrimmage produces a falsely-run race that suits hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: If Wild Nature fails to sustain the gallop and the prominent scrimmage produces a falsely-run race that suits hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Pace, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded prominent group produces early friction and a runner at big odds finds an uncontested lead or a clear split.
scenarios.body: If the crowded prominent group produces early friction and a runner at big odds finds an uncontested lead or a clear split.

watchPoints.text: Wild Nature (Oisin Murphy) is the entire pivot of this race — if it gets a clean break from the stalls and establishes its lead uncontested, the pace shape is set; watch whether any of the displaced prominent types (Golden Strike, Delinquent) attempt to press it early, which could turn the gallop injurious.

The cluster of prominent horses — Sujet, Jimmy Speaking, Frankies Dream, Zennor Storm and Blue To Blue — cannot all get the positions they want; crowding in the first two furlongs on the straight York mile could cause interference, shuffling, and a fractured pace that distorts the race entirely.

Golden Strike and Delinquent are both confirmed front-runners who will be unable to lead — watch their early behaviour from their draw, as a frustrated early rush by either could pressure Wild Nature and turn this into a genuine test that burns off the prominent horses.

Andesite (Kevin Stott) wears a tongue-tie and is stepping up in trip from 7f; if the race is run at a honest gallop through the middle stages, watch whether it can sustain its hold-up effort over the longer straight — a lack of finishing reserves at a mile could expose it late.

Darkness (Mark Winn) is a 7f specialist at age eight stepping up to a flat mile — if the race is run at a slow-to-moderate pace and compresses in the home straight, its finishing punch could be relevant, but jockey must find clear daylight early in the York straight given its deep hold-up position.

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Dash Handicap

runners_data.name: Manatee Mehmas
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner with a win over this exact course, distance and going last time; David Nolan likely to roll forward and control fractions, though tagged with a style-fit caution as the pace role requires him to sustain rather than quicken — his recent 4th and 8th suggest vulnerability if challenged late.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts ago and showed good prior form, but last time a step up to Listed grade at Sandown saw him well beaten by 7 lengths; returns to handicap company over 5f on a surface he handles well, though the official mark still looks demanding at this level.

runners_data.name: Boston Dan
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist from the Fahey yard running on the back of a string of mid-teen finishes; needs a truly run race to get competitive and his Good-ground record over five furlongs (0W3P) underlines how hard the task is from the back here.
runners_data.comment: Trailing the field last time here when making no impression from off the pace, beaten 7 lengths; winless in his last five outings and the mark, though easing, still looks stiff given how out of contention he has been in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Schrodinger's Cat
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a strong profile at this trip on good ground — 2 wins and 9 places from 12 good-ground starts is a standout stat; Grant Tuer's yard only 1/15 in the last fortnight but the horse's own form through the card is compelling.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap comfortably at Redcar last time, winning by 5 lengths off a mark 8lb lower than today's; effective at 5f on sound ground and reliable, but a quick turnaround and a stiffer mark here raise the bar considerably.

runners_data.name: Stargazed
runners_data.note: K R Burke's 3yo has ability but that run 12th last time on good ground raises a flag; returned a win on soft, suggesting better ground may blunt the finish, and this wide field at York makes prominent positioning trickier than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Posted a clear second here over this course and trip two starts ago, which is the key positive; she handles good to firm and rates a live contender returning to handicap company, though last time's well-beaten effort needs to be firmly reversed.

runners_data.name: Fortification
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison runner with consistent pattern — never far away, hits the frame regularly; won over 5f good ground two runs ago and finished second last time, making him a solid each-way profile in the prominent cluster.
runners_data.comment: Finished with real purpose when a close-up third over 6f last time, beaten only a length off a mark 3lb lower than today's; has a liking for this course and rates a prime threat here, though the trainer is in a lean spell and the weight rise is the main reservation.

runners_data.name: Our Cody
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes-trained 3yo who goes well fresh and has placed twice at this trip on good ground; Neil Callan's booking adds interest and a recent third suggests residual form, though nine starts at 5f/Good show only one win in that spot.
runners_data.comment: Fourth beaten just 1½ lengths in a Listed sprint last time showed her quality, and dropping back to handicap company off this mark is a clear step down in class; consistent and effective at 5f on good ground, she is a real threat, winless in her last five outings but well respected off this mark.

runners_data.name: Shes Got A Brother
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty-partnered 3yo who has been winning on standard and soft ground; only 2/5 on good in her history which tempers enthusiasm, and this is a tougher contest than her previous wins came in.
runners_data.comment: Progressive across her last five starts with two wins, she held her form well when beaten only 2 lengths in a Listed fillies' sprint last time; top of the ratings in this field and effective at 5f on good ground, she is the one to beat back in handicap company.

runners_data.name: Mighty Magnus
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type from Michael Dods' yard who won at 5f/Good last time and has two career wins at the trip; 21 days since that run is fine, and his last-to-first profile is realistic if the pace is strong enough to create a gap.
runners_data.comment: Landed his first handicap at Musselburgh last time by 1¼ lengths off a mark 5lb lower than today's; effective at 5-6f on good ground and capable when there is a pace to chase, though the step up in the weights here asks a fresh question.

runners_data.name: Naana's Shadow
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Katie Scott — a yard that has been quiet recently (0/8 T14) — and this filly boasts three wins over 5f, two on good ground; a natural front-runner in form terms, she'll need Murphy to position her prominently early despite the crowded pace map.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in her last five starts including a narrow success at Epsom last time off a mark 7lb lower than today's; progressive and effective at 5f on good ground, though the raised handicap mark is the main test now.

runners_data.name: Allsortz
runners_data.note: David Marnane's Irish raider has two wins on standard/soft ground but only 0W2P on Good, which is a concern; he races keenly and wants to be prominent, and with six horses competing for those early slots he may not get the position his style demands.
runners_data.comment: Beaten only a quarter of a length off his previous mark last time, he arrives in decent nick; effective across a range of trips from 5-7f and consistent enough, but our figures place him towards the lower end of the ratings here and a 2lb rise makes progress harder to find.

runners_data.name: Front Line Fury
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners this George Scott 3yo who has been finding the ends of fields recently (6th, 10th, 7th); his best form came at 6f on standard ground and the drop to 5f on good looks like it is going against him here — pushed towards midfield, he'll need a significant improvement.
runners_data.comment: Posted a personal-best effort when beaten 2½ lengths off this exact mark last time, showing he retains ability over 6f; a proven jockey at this venue boosts his claims and the going suits, but he needs to build on that improvement after a winless spell in recent outings.

runners_data.name: Go Vince Go
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 3yo has been finishing in mid-division consistently on good ground (8th, 8th, 3rd, 4th, 17th in last five); Sean Kirrane takes the ride and with his natural style unable to assert in this field, the task looks steep from where he'll realistically race.
runners_data.comment: Finished well adrift last time here, beaten 9 lengths and making no impression; the mark is easing but he has been winless in his last five starts and is bottom-rated in this field, requiring a significant step forward to feature.

runners_data.name: Hanney Girl
runners_data.note: The tongue-tie is on for Tim Easterby's filly who has four visits to 5f/Good with three placed runs but recent form has tailed off (9th, 5th, 7th, 6th); the headgear change is the angle to watch but prominent ground can't be guaranteed in this field.
runners_data.comment: Gave little in her last run at Epsom, beaten 4 lengths below her best off a mark just 1lb higher; the addition of a tongue-tie today may help, and she is capable at 5f on a sound surface, but questions remain over consistency.

runners_data.name: Alfa Duplicate
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's 3yo has won twice in recent months on softer surfaces (soft, standard) but has failed to place in two runs on good ground; De Sousa's booking lifts interest, but the going question is real and being pushed wider in the pack against her preferred style makes this tough.
runners_data.comment: Had three wins in her last six starts and had been running consistently until a well-beaten sixth last time off the same mark as today's; effective at 5-6f on good to soft and AW, but that latest dip makes her hard to fancy despite the strong recent profile.

runners_data.name: Rotokura Belle
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 5f on good ground for Ivan Furtado and Cam Hardie retains the ride; the hold-up profile means she needs a strong pace to materialise, but two wins on good ground and a seven-run good-ground sample (2W4P) shows she handles the conditions well.
runners_data.comment: Won here last time by a narrow margin off a mark 6lb lower than today's, which shows she handles this course and trip; suited to 5f on a sound surface, but form is inconsistent and the raised handicap mark now asks considerably more.

races.paceDynamic: Manatee Mehmas is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger looking to press hard from the gates, is set to dictate a controlled, measured gallop over York's straight five furlongs on good ground. Behind him, a cluster of prominent-style horses — Schrodinger's Cat, Stargazed, Fortification, Our Cody, and Shes Got A Brother — will jostle for the limited early positions just off the leader, creating a contested but not frenetic mid-pack. The hold-up runners Boston Dan, Mighty Magnus, and Rotokura Belle will be ridden to settle and deliver their challenge in the final furlong, though with a sustainable rather than scorching early pace their task is harder than ideal. This race shape — one uncontested leader, a compressed prominent group, and genuine closers — marginally favours horses racing prominently just off the pace who can benefit from a controlled tempo, rather than late finishers who need the race to be run truly fast. The field contains more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate: Naana's Shadow, Allsortz, Front Line Fury, Go Vince Go, Hanney Girl, and Alfa Duplicate are all natural prominent racers, but most will be shuffled back into midfield against their will — of those, Naana's Shadow (Oisin Murphy aboard) and Allsortz are best-credentialled to actually fight for and secure a prominent position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Manatee Mehmas leads at a sustainable gallop and the prominent chasers settle just off him cleanly.
scenarios.body: If Manatee Mehmas leads at a sustainable gallop and the prominent chasers settle just off him cleanly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Manatee Mehmas bowls along unchallenged and the prominent group fail to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Manatee Mehmas bowls along unchallenged and the prominent group fail to close the gap in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is deceptively quick despite appearances and the prominent group chase hard, leaving them vulnerable in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is deceptively quick despite appearances and the prominent group chase hard, leaving them vulnerable in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Prominent Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple natural prominent types force their way forward early, creating an unexpectedly contested pace that unravels the front group.
scenarios.body: If multiple natural prominent types force their way forward early, creating an unexpectedly contested pace that unravels the front group.

watchPoints.text: Naana's Shadow has Oisin Murphy in the saddle and strong winning form at 5f on good ground — watch whether Murphy forces her forward early to reclaim natural prominent position against the redistributed pace map, because if she gets the spot she's a serious player.

Manatee Mehmas sets the tempo for the entire field; if David Nolan is allowed to slip the field going to halfway unchallenged, the gap he creates may prove decisive — monitor how strong the early gallop actually is versus how controlled it looks.

Allsortz and Front Line Fury are both natural prominent types being mapped to midfield — if either fires forward from the gates and contests early positions, the pace dynamic changes materially and hold-up horses gain an unexpected advantage.

Mighty Magnus and Rotokura Belle are the two most credentialled hold-up horses and both have won at 5f on good ground recently; the key question is whether the sustained tempo is strong enough for them to pick up in the final furlong — watch their positions at halfway as a real-time tell.

Schrodinger's Cat's 12/12 good-ground record is a standout sample in this field; if she secures an uncontested prominent berth behind the leader, her proven ability to produce in these conditions makes her a consistent danger throughout the straight.

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Criterion Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Balmacara
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Eve Johnson Houghton who has placed twice in three similar-going runs at this trip, though wins have dried up (last win not visible in recent form); Clifford Lee has limited options tactically and will need the race to develop late.|
runners_data.comment: Effective at 7-10f on today's ground and a genuine threat at this level; his most recent run at Epsom was compromised by racing too freely, but a more settled display from draw 4 could see him perform much closer.

runners_data.name: Chicago Critic
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's five-year-old has an outstanding 13/15 record on Good ground and was runner-up last time out over this exact trip — Oisin Orr rides, headgear (p) suggests a freshened profile, and the hold-up style suits a controlled-pace scenario well.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Epsom last time on soft ground, performing to his usual level but beaten five lengths; winless in his last six and ranked fifth on our figures, though his Meydan form encourages and a trainer in good shape adds a touch of hope.

runners_data.name: Never So Brave
runners_data.note: The top-rated runner in the field at OR 115 with four wins in nine similar-going starts; Andrew Balding's Oisin Murphy booking is significant, and as the lone front-runner he will dictate the race's shape — his STYLE_FIT tag reflects that he is catalogued as Prominent rather than pure Leader, so there is a marginal note of caution about his lead credentials, but in practice he is the class front-runner here.|
runners_data.comment: Comfortably our top-rated, he carries clear excuses for both runs this season — failing to settle at a longer trip on reappearance, then soft ground at Epsom last time; back to 7f on a sound surface without a penalty, he should be much closer to his best.

runners_data.name: Qirat
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's consistent prominent type has been busy on softer ground but holds two wins from seven Good-ground runs; the tongue-tie flag and 22-day break are worth monitoring — Silvestre De Sousa will seek to position close enough to dominate the finish if the pace suits.|
runners_data.comment: Rated third here and capable on his day, he acts on any ground at 7-8f and adds a tongue-tie for the first time; a 9l beating at Epsom last time is concerning though, and his standout Group 1 effort from earlier sets a higher bar than anything he has shown this season.

runners_data.name: Royal Velvet
runners_data.note: William Knight's mare arrives on the back of two quick wins at this exact trip on Good ground and is in sparkling form — last run only 9 days ago speaks to her freshness — but she is a horse who wants to race close to the pace, and with Never So Brave and Saber Strike ahead of her in the queue, she may not get that position freely; her STYLE_FIT discount is real if she has to race further back than ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Three wins in her last five efforts proved strong prior form, but she was well off the pace and held last time; our figures place her sixth in the field and, with just nine days since that poor run, a quick bounce-back is essential.

runners_data.name: Saber Strike
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old is lightly raced but has won twice from three starts, both on Good ground at 6-7f — Tom Marquand takes the ride, and the horse's natural instinct to race prominently means he is the one most likely to push Never So Brave into a proper gallop; racing out of his preferred spot would blunt his chance, and his youth and inexperience at Group level add a layer of risk.|
runners_data.comment: Two consecutive wins prior to last week's Group 3, where he stepped up in grade and was well beaten; back on a quick turnaround carrying 9lb less than the top-rated with an accomplished jockey-trainer pairing at this venue, he remains a genuine danger at these weights.

races.paceDynamic: Never So Brave is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse keen to lead, will dictate from the front at a pace he chooses — almost certainly a steady-to-honest gallop on Good ground over seven furlongs at York. Saber Strike and Royal Velvet are both natural prominent racers who want to sit close to the pace, but this field contains more genuine pace-hungry types than can all occupy their preferred position; Never So Brave is near-certain to secure the lead, while Saber Strike — younger, fresher (7 days), and with two wins from three — is best-placed to press him from the front rank, leaving Royal Velvet most likely to be shuffled back from her natural position. The lone front-runner setting a controlled tempo on a flat, fair track creates a race that strongly favours hold-up horses with a finishing kick who can exploit any late tempo collapse, and prominent racers who can sit close enough to pounce — pure closers who need a true-run gallop to close the gap are better served here than in a muddling sprint, but the chief beneficiary is any horse capable of tracking and quickening off a controlled pace.

scenarios.title: Never So Brave Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Never So Brave sets an uncontested, controlled pace and kicks clear turning for home.
scenarios.body: If Never So Brave sets an uncontested, controlled pace and kicks clear turning for home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely steady and the field bunches, allowing true closers to sprint past a tired lead.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves genuinely steady and the field bunches, allowing true closers to sprint past a tired lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Grind — Saber Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Saber Strike pushes Never So Brave into a genuine pace battle and the race is run at a true clip throughout.
scenarios.body: If Saber Strike pushes Never So Brave into a genuine pace battle and the race is run at a true clip throughout.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Qirat Emerges Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart in the straight and Qirat, fresh from a 22-day break, finds a clear run to deliver his best late thrust.
scenarios.body: If the race falls apart in the straight and Qirat, fresh from a 22-day break, finds a clear run to deliver his best late thrust.

watchPoints.text: Never So Brave's ability to go unchallenged at the front is the single biggest factor — if Saber Strike presses him hard from the outset, the whole race shape changes and true hold-up closers like Chicago Critic become far more dangerous.

Royal Velvet arrives in brilliant form but was seen racing from stall 25 in her last run at York (a rough start) — watch the draw and early-gate behaviour here, as she cannot afford to miss the break if she is to secure her preferred prominent position in a six-runner field.

Saber Strike is only three and has just three career runs; at Group level over seven furlongs, an immature reaction to the occasion or a wide draw could compromise his chance of forcing the pace he needs to be at his best.

Chicago Critic's headgear flag (p — presumably a hood or ear coverings) is worth checking at the declaration stage — any equipment change in the paddock could indicate a shift in how Oisin Orr will deploy him tactically.

The Good going is confirmed consistently across all distances today at York, so no horse faces a ground concern — any horse previously labelled as performing better in softer conditions (Balmacara, whose five career similar-going runs are all on soft) may find this surface marginally less forgiving than their optimal.|

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Rock N Roll Pinkie
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here with solid Good-ground form, Silvestre De Sousa keeps it honest up front; confirmed prominent style suits this setup perfectly but must be respected as a potential front-end beneficiary rather than a winner outright given modest OR of 84.
runners_data.comment: Consistent at 14-16f on any ground and usually held up, she was comfortably outclassed stepping up to Group 3 level here last time; back in handicap company she is more at home, though the trainer's current poor run of form is a concern.

runners_data.name: Talismans Time
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's four-year-old returns from 62 days off having won twice in a short career over this sort of trip on Good ground; Cian Horgan's 5lb claim helps at the weights, and a forward-racing style means it will be ideally positioned if the pace is controlled.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time with something clearly amiss, all to prove on this return after over eight weeks away; his best form has come at shorter trips than today's 14f, which only adds to the uncertainty here.

runners_data.name: Secret Force
runners_data.note: Six days since last run is sharp enough to flag, but Adrian Paul Keatley has a decent 14-day strike rate and Secret Force's win over 1m6f on Good going is exactly the profile this race shape rewards; the hood (tv) may sharpen its early concentration in the prominent group.
runners_data.comment: Won at a longer trip last time and now drops to 14f — within his effective range — with the trainer in good form; a first-time tongue-tie and visor today, and the quick six-day turnaround is the only doubt about a horse who merits serious respect.

runners_data.name: Imperial Sovereign
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee partners this Philip Kirby hold-up type that has finished third twice at this sort of trip but struggles to convert from the rear; a zero from thirteen in the trainer's 14-day window is a note of caution, and pure hold-up reliance in a controlled-pace race over 1m6f at York is a difficult brief.
runners_data.comment: Placed twice over 12-16f on any ground in recent starts, he arrives 28 days after a 7-length defeat at Chester that was below his best; the mark is easing, but he needs to find significantly more to feature here.

runners_data.name: Gibside
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby saddles a well-travelled seven-year-old who has been running consistently without winning, and the 10/94 14-day trainer strike rate provides no strong angle; Good ground form is modest (10th last time over 1m6f) and a hold-up style here means it needs more pace than Rock N Roll Pinkie is likely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Posted his strongest effort of 2026 at Catterick 16 days ago, beaten only 3 lengths off a 2lb higher mark than today's; proven over extended trips on most surfaces and carrying a fair mark, he is a genuine contender despite a patchy recent record.

runners_data.name: Terrorise
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's five-year-old runs in a visor and has a grim recent sequence — its true running style is a genuine hold-up type that operates from well off the pace, but this race shape offers insufficient pace to bring it into play; finishing positions of 13th and 16th in recent Good-ground sprints/stays suggest confidence is not high.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five and usually held up, he was never competitive at Chester on his most recent outing and now returns after 50 days off wearing a visor for the first time; with the trainer badly out of form, he has much to prove.

runners_data.name: Draupnir
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up type by inclination — the horse's best form has come from off the pace over shorter trips (7f, 9f), and stepping up to 1m6f with handicap headgear (h) is a significant ask; Billy Garritty rides, and while the horse has placed form on Good ground, it is racing in an unfamiliar role at an unfamiliar distance.
runners_data.comment: Equipped with a first-time hood for today's big jump in trip, beaten three-quarters of a length at Hamilton last time; proven at 7-9f on today's going but this 14f task is well beyond his established range and stamina is the key doubt.

runners_data.name: My Ballyquinn
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old carries an unresolved style question (U) but recent 1m2f placed form on Good ground and a lightly-weighted 127lbs make it dangerous; Mark Winn partners, and the horse's consistent record (1W3P in last five on Good) suggests it handles conditions and could slot in prominently to good effect.
runners_data.comment: Finished a neck second on his most recent start, moving well before just failing to collar the leader; he takes a 4lb penalty but should see out the extra distance and his current form makes him one of the main dangers.

runners_data.name: Who's Lope
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on Andrew Balding's lightly-raced three-year-old who won over 1m2f and placed over 1m4f on Good ground — the profile is interesting and the step to 1m6f is the key unknown; small sample size (three runs) gives limited confidence, but the class handler and top jockey partnership merits respect.
runners_data.comment: Won last time by over four lengths, clearly improving as the trip increased, and a notable jockey booking adds appeal on his handicap debut over 14f; an opening mark of 83 looks fair and our rating places him at the head of this field.

races.paceDynamic: Rock N Roll Pinkie is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace rival likely to push hard from the outset, should be able to control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 1m6f trip on Good ground at York. Secret Force, Talismans Time, and to a lesser extent My Ballyquinn will press forward into prominent positions behind the leader, creating a competitive but not frantically-paced front group. The field carries more hold-up and off-pace types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Terrorise and Draupnir are genuine hold-up horses by inclination but are mapped to midfield given the distribution; neither is likely to find the truly wide-open late ground that their best form demands. With one uncontested front-runner setting a controlled pace over a staying distance, this race shape heavily favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort, as closers dependent on a truly fierce gallop will find conditions less than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Prominent Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Rock N Roll Pinkie leads at a fair but unhurried pace and the prominent trio close the gap smoothly in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Rock N Roll Pinkie leads at a fair but unhurried pace and the prominent trio close the gap smoothly in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Breaks Prominent Hold
scenarios.trigger: If Rock N Roll Pinkie goes quick enough early to string out the field and leave the prominent horses emptying late.
scenarios.body: If Rock N Roll Pinkie goes quick enough early to string out the field and leave the prominent horses emptying late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Sticks At Honest Price
scenarios.trigger: If Rock N Roll Pinkie's experienced front-running is underestimated and the pace is truly sedate, allowing it to steal an unassailable lead.
scenarios.body: If Rock N Roll Pinkie's experienced front-running is underestimated and the pace is truly sedate, allowing it to steal an unassailable lead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Arrive Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely muddling and closers are left with too much to do despite a tardy tempo.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely muddling and closers are left with too much to do despite a tardy tempo.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Talismans Time bounces back sharp enough from a 62-day absence — if it does recapture the winning form shown over similar trips on Good ground, it is directly in the wheel of the pace and will be very hard to peg back.

Secret Force ran just six days ago; monitor its early movement for any sign of staleness, as a prominent horse that ties up at York over 1m6f will leave the door wide open for Who's Lope to sweep through late.

Draupnir's headgear (h, hood) and step from 7-9f on the Flat to 1m6f is a dramatic profile shift — watch how Billy Garritty places it in the early stages, as a horse used to racing over a mile shorter could be caught cold by the pace or conversely bolt up early and die.

Who's Lope represents the classic Oisin Murphy/Andrew Balding staying three-year-old angle — only three career runs means the market and pace map have limited data to work with, so any significant market move approaching the off deserves attention.

Rock N Roll Pinkie's ability to control the pace without being pressed is the single most important variable in this race — if anything forces it wide or pushes early, the entire dynamic shifts toward hold-up horses arriving late on a fast-run track.

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Sprint Handicap

runners_data.name: Evening Blues
runners_data.note: Consistent performer at this age with placed efforts in similar conditions, suits a prominent handy position just off the leader on Good ground over this 6f, but recent form shows a slight drop in sparkle and the step into a 15-runner field at York adds positional complexity.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Musselburgh last time and ranked 13th on our figures, he drops to 6f today wearing a hood for the first time; the trip change is an interesting switch for a horse effective at 7-8f, though more is required to reverse recent form.

runners_data.name: Kinnalargy
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up type with a best effort of third over 6f on Good going; drawn in a big field and ridden by Oisin McSweeney, the key is whether a controlled pace allows enough of a final-furlong surge to make up ground.
runners_data.comment: Beaten only two lengths off a mark 1lb higher than today's at Thirsk last time, showing a return to form that makes him a contender at 5-6f on a sound surface; the trainer's recent run has been lean and he is yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Hallo Spaceboy
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on this Ed Walker three-year-old who is a natural prominent racer with solid Good-ground form, including a win over 5f on a similar surface; a 50-day break is a mild flag, but Walker's yard is in decent recent nick and the horse has winning course-distance profile.
runners_data.comment: Top of our ratings for this 15-runner sprint, he ran a determined race at Ascot last time — beaten only a neck off a 5lb lower mark — and returns from 50 days away with a notable jockey upgrade; a progressive profile suggests he can take a forward step.

runners_data.name: Rikki Tiki Tavi
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won over 5f on Good but has struggled since, including three consecutive double-figure finishes in his most recent attempts; a 70-day break is a concern, and he needs a much stronger pace than Percy's Star is likely to produce to bring his finishing kick into play.
runners_data.comment: Three consecutive unplaced outings most recently, including trailing the field at Thirsk on the latest, and off a two-month break; the mark has been dropping but much more is needed, even on ground that suits at 5-6f.

runners_data.name: Invincible Boy
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's colt has a tidy three-race record with a win and a placed effort, and the prominent style suits this race shape well; the 81-day absence is the main query, but the form profile over 6f on Good ground is directly relevant.
runners_data.comment: Won a novice last time by over two lengths and has more to offer on his first handicap start; he acts on heavy and good ground over 6f and is a genuine danger, though the 11-week absence is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Arduis Invicta
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's hold-up type has a frustrating record of near-misses and placed efforts in similar conditions, though a string of sixth-place finishes on identical going suggests he finds one or two too good rather than running badly; William Pyle's experience in large-field handicaps will be tested here.
runners_data.comment: Second at Musselburgh last time, beaten only 1¼ lengths off this mark, and the return to 6f is a positive development given her effective range; yet to score in recent starts but she ran with consistency and has realistic claims here.

runners_data.name: Vidmiyr
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's three-year-old is a prominent type who has placed on Good ground and is fresh off a 15-day break; the drop from mile-plus trips to 6f is an interesting trainer move, and a small stable enjoying a decent T14 strike rate adds mild interest.
runners_data.comment: Just denied at Chester last time in soft conditions, going down by a head off a mark 2lb below today's; today's drop to 6f is a new angle for a horse more established at 7-8f, and while consistent, he sits mid-field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Bleep Test
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's two-year-old returns after a massive 345-day layoff having finished last season with good form including a win over 6f; prominent style fits perfectly, but the rust from such a long absence in a competitive 15-runner handicap is a significant practical concern.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a 345-day absence, making this essentially a fitness run; her last outing before the layoff was below form and the trainer's current strike rate is poor, though she is effective at 5-6f and should come on for the run.

runners_data.name: Mr Noble
runners_data.note: K R Burke's colt has only two runs to his name — a win and a placed effort over 6f at Southwell — making him unknown at York on Good turf; Clifford Lee takes the ride and the prominent style suits, but the limited profile makes class assessment difficult.
runners_data.comment: Made a winning debut before finishing runner-up at Wolverhampton last time, confirming early promise on the all-weather; he makes his turf debut today in a handicap and further progress is expected, though the switch to grass is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Million Gold
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's three-year-old is genuinely a prominent-style horse by inclination, but with the prominent berths over-subscribed in this 15-runner field he is likely to find himself further back than ideal; Tom Marquand is a strong booking, and the horse has winning form, but racing out of his natural position tempers expectations meaningfully.
runners_data.comment: Won a novice before a 4-length third at Newcastle last time, where he had every chance; first-time cheekpieces and a proven jockey at this track are strong positives here, and he is lightly raced with more to offer after a long break.

runners_data.name: Percy's Star
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, and Silvestre De Sousa should ensure he controls the pace from the outset on a flat 6f at York; an uncontested lead on Good ground suits this profile ideally, and recent improvement is backed by a win first time out over 5f on similar terms.
runners_data.comment: Got off the mark by 3½ lengths at Leicester last time at 5f, showing improvement, but steps up to 6f today off a mark 8lb higher; first-time cheekpieces are a plus and he looks progressive, though the significant rise in his official rating is the main challenge.

runners_data.name: Explosive Finnish
runners_data.note: Kevin and Lauren Frost's hold-up horse has a consistent record of placed efforts without winning, suggesting a reliable but limited ceiling; a 15-day turnaround keeps him fresh, and he needs a strongly-run race to get competitive from his rearward position.
runners_data.comment: Beaten only three-quarters of a length at Chester last time when upped to 6f, performing consistently to his level; with a trainer in decent form, he is yet to score in his last five but continues to compete at this level, even if a 2lb higher mark makes it no easier.

runners_data.name: Logi Bear
runners_data.note: John Butler's runner is a genuine hold-up type by nature but the map places him in midfield given the congestion of closers in this field; recent form is modest with consecutive poor finishes, and Marco Ghiani will need a completely different kind of run to unlock any improvement here.
runners_data.comment: Second at Thirsk last time, beaten a length off a mark 1lb lower than today's, offering encouragement after a run of poor efforts; suited by 6f on ground with some give and usually held up, he warrants consideration if reproducing that effort.

runners_data.name: Bye Law
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's runner is by inclination a prominent racer, but with too many rivals wanting the same ground he is displaced into midfield on the race map; Cam Hardie has placed efforts over this course and distance on Good, and a 10-day turnaround suggests yard confidence, though racing further back than ideal is a genuine disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Third at Ripon last time beaten 1¼ lengths off this mark, though a run of inconsistency makes him hard to assess; first-time cheekpieces today and running off a competitive weight, he is yet to score in recent starts and needs to find more.

runners_data.name: Von Trotter
runners_data.note: Michael and David Easterby's hold-up type has been struggling for form, with a string of poor finishes on Good ground including several over this course configuration; a very recent run just eight days ago is notable, and James Sullivan will need significant improvement from this 65-rated runner to make an impact.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Redcar last time in a performance short of his earlier form, and he returns on only eight days' rest; best suited to front-running on the all-weather, today's turf conditions ask different questions — ranked at the foot of our figures here.

races.paceDynamic: Percy's Star is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, Silvestre De Sousa should be able to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on a flat, fair York 6f. The prominent group is heavily congested — Evening Blues, Hallo Spaceboy, Invincible Boy, Vidmiyr, Bleep Test and Mr Noble all want to sit just off the pace, creating a real danger of scrimmaging and traffic problems between the 2f and 3f markers as riders jockey for position behind a single front-runner. The field contains more pace than the map can accommodate: Million Gold and Bye Law are genuine prominent-type horses displaced into midfield on the race shape, and Percy's Star is the one most likely to secure the rail and dictate unchallenged. With one horse controlling a modest, uncontested gallop and a wall of prominent horses immediately behind, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in the first two or three, conserve energy in the slipstream, and produce a sustained finish — pure hold-up closers face the dual risk of traffic and a pace that may not be truly severe enough to reel in the leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Percy's Star Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Star bowls clear uncontested and sets an even, controlled pace that suits horses travelling just behind.
scenarios.body: If Percy's Star bowls clear uncontested and sets an even, controlled pace that suits horses travelling just behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion resolves quickly and two or three horses press Percy's Star hard enough to produce a truly run race.
scenarios.body: If the prominent congestion resolves quickly and two or three horses press Percy's Star hard enough to produce a truly run race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Untangles Late
scenarios.trigger: If the midfield congestion between 2f and 3f out causes significant interference and leaves one or two horses with late, clear daylight.
scenarios.body: If the midfield congestion between 2f and 3f out causes significant interference and leaves one or two horses with late, clear daylight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsiders Steal Unnoticed
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Star is allowed such a soft lead that the race develops slowly and a prominent type sprints clear while fancied rivals are caught flat-footed.
scenarios.body: If Percy's Star is allowed such a soft lead that the race develops slowly and a prominent type sprints clear while fancied rivals are caught flat-footed.

watchPoints.text: Percy's Star (De Sousa) could dictate the entire race from the front — watch for whether any of the prominent group immediately challenges or whether he steals a soft lead unchallenged in the first furlong.

The prominent group — Evening Blues, Hallo Spaceboy, Invincible Boy, Vidmiyr, Bleep Test and Mr Noble — will create a scrimmage between 3f and 2f out; any horse caught wide or pocketed here could have their chance effectively ended, watch draw positions carefully at the off.

Bleep Test returns from 345 days off for Easterby — watch the market move and early behaviour in the parade; a prominent runner fresh from such a long break in a fast-breaking 15-runner sprint is unpredictable.

Million Gold and Bye Law are natural prominent types mapped to midfield — if either fails to secure a forward position in the early stages, watch whether they can still travel efficiently from a deeper than ideal slot or whether they fade into the pack.

Hallo Spaceboy (50-day break, Oisin Murphy) is worth monitoring pre-race for any market support — Murphy rarely takes rides in 0-85 handicaps without stable confidence, and the horse's Good-ground profile is directly on point.

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Amateur Jockeys' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Hengest
runners_data.note: Won twice over 10-12f on Good ground recently and carries the prominent-racer tag accurately here as the race's only genuine pace-setter; Dylan Cunha's small string has landed 2 from 29 over 14 days, last ran 21 days ago, and with blinkers on this is a horse that must be respected if it softens rivals up from the front.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five efforts proved strong prior form, but last time on softer ground he was well beaten; returning to faster going here and fitted with cheekpieces for the first time, the return to preferred conditions makes him a significant threat despite the same mark.

runners_data.name: Machete
runners_data.note: David O'Meara hold-up specialist who has run exclusively on Southwell's Tapeta in its last five starts, none on Good ground, giving a stark going concern over this surface; 57 days off the track, and the 12f trip is familiar but the form line of 0W0P on similar-going reads bleakly.
runners_data.comment: Absent for nearly two months and disappointing on his most recent start at Newcastle, beaten 15 lengths; arguably best beyond today's 10f trip and needing to rediscover his form back on turf after a break, he is an uncertain proposition despite the longer distance being a potential positive.

runners_data.name: Midnight Strike
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's hold-up type whose recent form has been run entirely at 7f on Good, finishing well down the field each time; stepping up markedly to 1m2½f today on the same trainer's 2/23 14-day record, and the 13-13-13 placings over sprint trips suggest this trip is entirely unexplored territory.
runners_data.comment: Out of the places in his last four outings and well behind when uncompetitive here last time, he also faces a question over whether he will see out 10f for the first time; best at 6-7f with cut, today is a significant challenge for a horse who has been winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Double Parked
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 4yo has placed three times over 8f on Good and carries tongue-tie headgear as a repeat aid; races prominently at a natural gallop, last ran 8 days ago suggesting freshness isn't an issue, and this step to 1m2½f is the key question — but 3/8f on Good twice suggests it stays and should handle the extra ground.
runners_data.comment: Beaten only a head last time when tried in a tongue-tie, showing his current form is solid; he enjoys setting the pace and acts on sound ground, and the tongue-tie continues today, though stamina for the step up to 10f remains the key question.

runners_data.name: Ben Lawers
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's 4yo races prominently and has shown 1W2P in similar going, though all five recent runs show it performing best at 8f on Tapeta/Standard; today's Good ground at 1m2½f is a different proposition, 48 days off adding a fitness query, and the tongue-tie is a returning aid worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Pulled hard at Leopardstown last time and was beaten 5 lengths, having taken a strong hold; consistent enough in terms of form but returning after 48 days off, and the addition of a tongue-tie today suggests connections are looking to settle him, which remains the key risk.

runners_data.name: Spirit Genie
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's 6yo runs from the back and has form figures of 0W0P on similar going with recent efforts at 7f on Soft or Good; the step to 1m2½f is significant and there is nothing in the hist line to encourage confidence at this trip or on this surface, making visor headgear the only fresh variable.
runners_data.comment: Out of the action last time at Chester, beaten 7½ lengths from off the pace, and now tried in both a tongue-tie and visor for the first time; winless in his last five starts with the extra distance unproven, stepping up considerably beyond his most effective range.

runners_data.name: Pearl Eye
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's hold-up type who has won and placed multiple times over 9f on Good ground, making the going and trip combination the most appealing fit in the field for a closer; 14 days since last run is manageable, amateur claim of 5lb helps, and the 1W3P on similar going underpins its place in the frame discussion.
runners_data.comment: Third last time beaten only three-quarters of a length off a mark 1lb lower than today's, he arrives in fine fettle; first-time cheekpieces add a further angle and the return to 10f should suit, making him a leading danger in this field.

runners_data.name: Glistening Nights
runners_data.note: Fahey's 5yo is naturally a hold-up horse — it has placed twice over 10f on Good — but with so many closers in this field it ends up mapped in midfield, a position that does not reflect its instinctive race-from-rear style; its best recent form came over 10f on similar ground and the 2/10f Good win is the strongest pace-map credential in the hold-up group.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten here last time but clearly capable at 10f on a sound surface, which is exactly what today's conditions offer; two decent placed efforts in his last five starts suggest ability is present, though he needs to bounce back sharply from that disappointing run.

runners_data.name: Urban Road
runners_data.note: Alan Brown's 7yo is a genuine hold-up operator whose trainer has 0/8 over 14 days, and it races here having been bumped forward in the map due to overcrowding at the rear; its recent 2nd and 3rd over 10f on Good are solid but the race shape — with so many closers seeking the same late run — limits its chances structurally.
runners_data.comment: Pulled hard and well out of contention last time here; winless in his last six starts and among the lower-ranked in this field, he needs a significant rebound to feature, though he has been placed at this trip and the going suits.

runners_data.name: Caph Star
runners_data.note: Mark Rimell's 7yo races prominently and has won over 10f on Good, giving it genuine course-type credentials; 24 days since last run, 0/5 for the trainer over 14 days, but 1W2P on similar going and a consistent record at this distance makes it a legitimate target for the prominent scenario.
runners_data.comment: Moving in the right direction when fifth beaten 4¼ lengths last time off a mark 1lb higher than today's; fitted with a tongue-tie for the first time here and effective at 8-11f, but still needs more to get involved and remains towards the foot of the ratings.

runners_data.name: No Knee Never
runners_data.note: James Owen's 5yo (T14: 9/49, one of the busiest in the race) races from a prominent pitch with tongue-tie and hood headgear; it has placed twice over 10f on Good but its win came at 8f on Standard, and the 14-day record suggests this yard fires its horses in and ready — a small but real positive factor.
runners_data.comment: Effective across a range of trips including 10f, he arrives with first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces applied, which could sharpen him up; last time he was well beaten off a mark 1lb lower and still operates 5lb above his last winning level, making the gear changes the key angle to follow.

runners_data.name: Theme Park
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's 5yo is a hold-up type by nature, pushed into a midfield slot due to the volume of closers in this field — the race map position is not its natural home; 232 days off the track is the single most alarming stat in the race, and while it has placed at 8-10f on Good, that layoff makes this a speculative reappearance.
runners_data.comment: Absent for more than seven months, which is the overriding concern on return here; last run saw him well beaten by 8 lengths in a handicap, and winless in his last five outings he needs considerable improvement to feature despite the drop in the weights.

runners_data.name: Spirit Catcher
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's 7yo has won and placed at 9-12f on Good and is a genuine rear-of-field operator who has been mapped forward due to the overcrowded hold-up group; its 1W3P on similar going is genuinely competitive and, if it can secure a passage through, it represents one of the more capable true closers despite the trainer's 0/16 in 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Eighth last time and well beaten from off the pace, yet the step back up to a longer trip here is a genuine positive given he is effective at 8-12f on any ground; rated an outsider here but the trip brings out the best in him and he remains capable.

runners_data.name: Sisterandbrother
runners_data.note: Joey Ramsden's 8yo has won twice and placed twice over 11-12f on Good, the most prolific winning record in this field at the right trip and going combination; racing prominently from 137lbs at OR 61 in an amateur context, the weight concession to rivals is significant but the track-and-distance form on Good makes it a durable each-way prospect.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last six starts show he is capable in this sphere, but last time saw him well beaten in fifth, 6½ lengths adrift off a mark 1lb lower than today's; effective at 10-12f and handles the going, though bottom-rated here and needing more to figure.

races.paceDynamic: Hengest is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push him from the front, he is expected to bowl along at a sustainable, self-regulated gallop over this 1m2½f trip on Good ground at York. Double Parked, Ben Lawers, Caph Star, No Knee Never and Sisterandbrother will press for prominent positions behind him, creating a compact, organised early order rather than a scramble. The field does contain more hold-up horses than the pace map can honestly place at the rear — Glistening Nights, Urban Road, Theme Park and Spirit Catcher are true closers who have been redistributed into midfield slots, meaning the backmarkers are less populated and the midfield is busier than it appears. With one controlled pace-setter and a genuine surfeit of hold-up types forced to race closer than ideal, this race shape squarely favours horses racing prominently in behind Hengest — tracking a genuine but unhurried gallop and possessing the stamina to grind out the 1m2½f distance on a fair surface.

watchPoints.text: Hengest is the sole pace-setter in this 14-runner field — if Mr Fletcher Yarham elects to press on unchallenged early, watch for the tempo to drop deceptively low and catch the midfield flat-footed rounding the bend.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Glistening Nights, Urban Road, Theme Park and Spirit Catcher — are all seeking the same late run from a midfield position that is not their natural home; watch for traffic and interference in the straight as they converge on the same gaps.

Theme Park returns after 232 days off the track for Nigel Tinkler; watch for signs of race-rustiness in the first half, particularly at a trip (8f) shorter than its recent optimal, and factor that lay-off into any late-race assessment.

Pearl Eye, the most convincing hold-up horse with genuine 1W3P form at this trip and going, is partnered by a 5lb-claiming amateur (Miss Kayleigh Williams) — watch whether the claim offsets the positioning challenge from the rear and whether she can find a clean run from the 1m2½f start at York.

Tim Easterby's Double Parked last ran just 8 days ago and races prominently with tongue-tie; watch the market for any drift that might signal whether the quick turnaround has taken its toll, given it steps up to 1m2½f having not previously won beyond 8f.
